results.name: FT: Arsenal 3-2 Liverpool, Bukayo Saka Bags BRACE! (VIDEO HIGHLIGHTS)
results.content:
**Bukayo Saka scored a brace as Arsenal beat Liverpool 3-2 to move back to top of the Premier League table, MySportDab reports.**  
**First Half Report**  
Both teams had a fair enough opportunities of making something happen for themselves going forward in the 45 minutes seen between them.  
Arsenal scored the opening goal under few seconds from kickoff which saw Gabriel Martinelli finishing off neatly to make it 1-0 for the Gunners which was a perfect start for them.  
The game continued with Liverpool fighting to make a comeback which didn’t happen immediately as they had to wait until 34th minutes of the game to make something happen thanks to Darwin Nunez who made it 1-1.  
There was so much happenings with the game approaching the regular time conclusion which saw the referee signal for additional time with scoreline still the same but thanks to Bukayo Saka tap in, the Gunner took a 2-1 lead.  
The 45th-minute plus added-time goal was the last kick of the first half which came to an end with Arsenal taking a 2-1 lead into the break against Liverpool who wasn’t solid enough to stop the late finish.  
**Second Half Report**  
The second half started well with so much coming from both teams who came in knowing there is still a lot of work for them to do if they are going to end up with something good.
Arsenal was looking good and calm in the first few minutes of the second half which saw their opponent flooding in their defense to make sure something happens but it all was for nothing.  
Liverpool leveled things in the 53rd minute thanks to an outstanding finish which came from Roberto Firmino as the game went level 2-2 with more opportunities coming through for them.  
The Gunners took the lead once again thanks to Bukayo Saka stunning penalty kick which came after a foul ahe England International wasted no time in making it 3-2 in the 76th minute of the game.  
That goal ended things between them as Arsenal claimed a 3-2 win against Liverpool which sends them back to the top of the Premier League table.

results.name: Relentless Bukayo Saka Shines Again - But Arsenal Still Falter
results.content:
[Paris Saint-Germain knocked Arsenal out](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/07/they-were-in-tears-arteta-says-arsenal-squad-emotional-after-champions-league-exit)of the UEFA Champions League by winning the second leg of their semifinal 2-1 in Paris on Wednesday, May 7.  
PSG had earlier won the first leg, too, and progressed to the final with a 3-1 aggregate win.  
The victory for Luis Enrique’s men means that [Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal will have to finish yet another season without a silverware](https://www.nowarsenal.com/latest-news/martin-odegaard-admits-painful-truth-after-arsenals-champions-league-exit/).  
Arteta has won a solitary FA Cup with the Gunners in his six years as their manager, which is not a very encouraging piece of statistics.
## Bukayo Saka: Arsenal’s Consistent Force  
Bukayo Saka scored the only goal for Arsenal on Wednesday. The 23-year-old right-winger has 12 goals and 13 assists in 34 matches, which means that he is probably the best-performing player for the Gunners this season.  
In fact, [Saka’s injury in the middle of the season](https://extratimetalk.com/arsenal-injury-changed-season/) was one of the main reasons why his team fell behind in the race for the Premier League table.  
Arsenal failed to replace him properly, with a very young Ethan Nwaneri coming up with some decent performance while playing on the right flank and Leandro Trossard failing to shine in the same position.  
His return from injury has enabled the Gunners to perform better almost immediately.  
Saka is one of the more experienced players for the Gunners, despite being quite young. He has played in 260 matches for the North Londoners and scored 70 goals in them.  
He has been the mainstay of Arsenal’s attack along with Martin Odegaard for quite some time now.  
Aside from that, the [young Englishman has been one of the most consistent performers](https://extratimetalk.com/brililant-bukayo-saka-justifies-gareth-southgates-faith-in-him/) for the national team as well.  
**YOU MAY ALSO LIKE**: [Inter Milan One Step Away From Glorious European Triumph](https://extratimetalk.com/inter-milan-one-step-glorious-european-triumph/)
## Will Saka Move to Another Club in the Future?  
Saka is about to complete seven seasons at Arsenal.  
His contract expires in 2027 and it will be interesting to see if he moves to another club in the pursuit of a title. Saka will only be 25 at the time his contract with Arsenal expires.  
Someone like Trent Alexander-Arnold has severed his ties with Liverpool despite winning a few titles for the Reds and Saka could take a cue from him.  
Hence, Saka cannot be blamed if he harbours the ambition of winning trophies as a player. He can still do that while playing for Arsenal, but the chances appear somewhat slim at the moment, especially given their recent record.  
Arteta’s men have almost made it a habit to finish second in the Premier League and do not seem strong enough to win a European trophy either.  
Unless things change drastically, they might not be able to end their trophy drought next season either.  
Will Saka continue to be in the team when his current contract expires?

On 29 August 2020, Saka was in the starting line-up and registered an assist for Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang in the 2020 FA Community Shield, in which 2019–20 FA Cup winners Arsenal clinched a 5–4 penalty shoot-out victory over 2019–20 Premier League winners Liverpool, after the match finished 1–1 after 90 minutes. Saka opened his account for the 2020–21 season on 4 October, scoring in a 2–1 victory against Sheffield United at the Emirates Stadium. On 8 November, Saka turned in Matt Targett's cross and scored an own goal in a 3–0 home defeat against Aston Villa.
He scored first goal of the season in a 3–1 away defeat against Manchester United on 4 September. In their next Premier League match on 18 September, Saka would provide two assists for teammates William Saliba and Fábio Vieira in a 3–0 away victory at Brentford, a result that would sent Arsenal to the top of the table. Bukayo Saka has scored 12 goals for Arsenal across all competitions during the 2023-2024 season, according to a video compilation released by the club on June 17, 2026. The footage, titled “Every Bukayo Saka goal for The Arsenal,” highlights his contributions to the team’s attack, including crucial strikes in Premier League matches and European competitions. The video was shared on Arsenal.com, the club’s official website, and has since garnered widespread attention from fans and media outlets.
## Context of Saka’s Rise at Arsenal  
Saka, who joined Arsenal from the club’s academy in 2018, has gradually transitioned from a winger to a central attacking role. His versatility and technical skills have made him a key figure in Mikel Arteta’s tactical setup. During the 2023-2024 season, Saka averaged 0.8 shots per game and 1.2 key passes per match, according to Opta data. His ability to cut inside from the left flank and his composure in front of goal have been cited as factors in his goal-scoring consistency.  
Manager Mikel Arteta has frequently praised Saka’s work ethic and leadership. In a press conference on May 20, 2024, Arteta stated, “Bukayo’s development this season has been exceptional. He’s not just scoring goals; he’s driving the team forward with his energy and decision-making.” The manager also highlighted Saka’s role in Arsenal’s attacking philosophy, which prioritizes possession and quick transitions.  
Saka’s goal-scoring record is particularly notable given the competition for places in Arsenal’s forward line. Alongside Gabriel Jesus and Eddie Nketiah, Saka has maintained a strong presence in the starting XI. His 12 goals placed him second on the club’s scoring charts, behind Jesus’s 15 goals. This achievement marks a significant milestone in Saka’s career, as he continues to establish himself as a top-tier striker.
## Impact on Arsenal’s Season  
Saka’s contributions were instrumental in Arsenal’s pursuit of their first Premier League title since 2004. The team finished the 2023-2024 season with 78 points, securing second place behind Manchester City. Saka’s goals often came in critical moments, such as a late winner against West Ham United on April 22, 2024, which kept Arsenal in the title race until the final weeks of the campaign.  
His performances also played a role in Arsenal’s run to the UEFA Champions League semifinals. Saka scored a brace in a 3-2 victory over Barcelona in the quarterfinals, including a stunning long-range effort that was later named Goal of the Tournament by UEFA. The club’s official website noted that Saka’s “clutch performances” were a key factor in their European success.  
Despite the team’s failure to clinch the Premier League title, Saka’s individual achievements have drawn comparisons to past Arsenal legends. Former midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, who played for the club from 2003 to 2011, remarked in a post-match interview, “Bukayo is the kind of player who can carry a team. His consistency and maturity at such a young age are remarkable.”

results.name: Bukayo Saka's top ten Arsenal goals including screamer against Manchester United
results.content:
**Bukayo Saka has scored some stunning goals for Arsenal since breaking into the first team in late 2019.**  
The Hale End [Academy](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/club/academy/) graduate has enjoyed a meteoric rise at [the Emirates](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/club/stadium/), starting his career as a left-back and developing into one of the best wingers in world football.  
Unfortunately for [Mikel Arteta](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/tag/mikel-arteta/), [Saka underwent hamstring surgery](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/news/when-arsenal-actually-think-bukayo-saka-will-return-from-injury-as-timeframe-hope-emerges/) in December, and has subsequently missed a large portion of the 2024/25 season.  
This has prevented him from adding to his glorious goal catalogue, which currently contains 67 strikes in an [Arsenal](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/club/) shirt.  
Here are his top ten.
## 10 – vs Nottingham Forest (2024/25)  
Collecting the ball inside the box from an intricate [Martin Odegaard](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/tag/martin-odegaard/) pass, [Saka tip toed around Nottingham Forest’s defenders](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/match-reports/arsenal-fans-have-a-lot-to-say-as-bukayo-saka-scores-incredible-goal-they-love-what-one-teammate-did/), before digging a sensational effort out from under his feet.  
The ball nestled beyond Matz Sels in the Forest goal, opening the scoring in a tight game.  
The close control inside the box was mesmerising, making this one of [Saka’s](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/tag/bukayo-saka/) very best strikes.
## 5 – vs Liverpool (2024/25)  
In a huge game earlier this season, [Saka broke the deadlock](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/match-reports/arsenal-player-ratings-vs-liverpool-bukayo-saka-proves-hes-world-class-as-unsung-hero-gets-8-10/) with an outstanding goal against league leaders Liverpool.  
Played in over the top by [Ben White](https://www.arsenalinsider.com/tag/ben-white/), he took the ball down majestically, cut inside and nutmegged Andy Robertson, and roofed the ball into the net.
